_comment: SYS test points: the front- and rear-panel rows of Table 4-3 (p42 / 4-18) as
the instrument's own probe targets, plus the A3 and A4 rows of the same table
as system-level copies (A3TP1-6, A4TP1-3) so the whole Table 4-3 sweep can be
walked and logged from the interconnect view. The board's own point is the
authority for anything beyond Table 4-3; each copy links to it.
Table 4-3 prints no tolerance for 32 V, 33.0 V or 18.5 V. Those carry an
assumed tolerance marked inferred:true, copied from the board's own point so
the two datasets agree: 5 % (1.6 V) on the two 32 V rows, 0.5 V on the 33.0 V
set point (A3 TP5) and 0.5 V on the ~18.5 V row (A4 TP1). The output tolerances come
from Table 1-2's one-year transfer uncertainty and are marked inferred too:
they are a specification of drift, not a pass/fail limit the manual states.
Every voltage is signed positive as printed (HI with respect to LO). Where
the manual prints <= / >= the one-sided max / min form is used.
Engine note: a point attaches to a procedure step when its source cites
'step N' and the step names it in refs; the Table 4-3 procedure is id 4-3.

testpoints.note: Black binding post (Table 5-1 E4/E5) that is the common for the 10V output; fed from A5 E26 (through the term strip), E27 and E28 by harness W3. Table 4-3 writes it COM. The low lead for OUT10V. §4-4: use low-thermal lugs clamped in the post, tighten only with finger pressure.

testpoints.source: Table 2-1 item 12 (p16); Table 4-3 "COM" (p42); Figure 8-1 "LO" from E36 (p85)
testpoints.note: The second black binding post, common for the 1V and 1.018V outputs; fed from the divider LO, A5 E36, by harness W3. The low lead for OUT1V and OUT1018. Figure 5-1 Detail I does not say which of E4/E5 it is. Figure 8-1 simplifies the panel to a single LO terminal with E36, E26, E27 and E28 all bussed to it; Figure 8-5 keeps E36 (divider LO) separate from E26-E28 and the panel has two black posts (Table 2-1 items 11, 12).

testpoints.condition: IN CAL lit; powered continuously (line or battery); 23 ± 5 °C; no load (10V output 12 mA max)
testpoints.source: Table 4-3 front panel row, Internal voltage measurements step 7 (p42); tolerance from Table 1-2 transfer uncertainty, 10V, 1 year: 6.0 ppm (p10)
testpoints.note: Table 4-3 prints 10.00000V dc and no tolerance; ±6 ppm (±60 µV) is the one-year transfer uncertainty of Table 1-2 and is used here as the widest published figure - the 30-day figure is 0.5 ppm (±5 µV), 90 days 1.5 ppm, 6 months 3.0 ppm. The reading is only as good as the meter: Table 4-3's Multimeter A (4½ digits) cannot resolve it, Multimeter B (6½ digits, 100 µV resolution on 10 V) barely; a real verification is the null comparison of §4-37 / §4-39. §4-30 step 5: under a 1000 Ω load the change must be less than 50 µV (5.0 ppm). The 10V adjustment (A5 R20, front-panel hole) affects the 1.018V and 1V outputs and is made first (Table 2-1 footnote).

testpoints.condition: IN CAL lit; 10V output calibrated first; 23 ± 5 °C
testpoints.source: Table 4-3 front panel row, Internal voltage measurements step 8 (p42); tolerance from Table 1-2 transfer uncertainty, 1V, 1 year: 12.0 ppm (p10)
testpoints.note: Table 4-3 prints 1.000000V dc, corrective action Output Divider***. Footnote ***: calibration of the 10V output affects calibration of this output - check and set 10V first. ±12 ppm (±12 µV) is Table 1-2's one-year transfer uncertainty (30 days: 1.5 ppm); it is a drift specification, not a printed test limit. Source impedance ≈1 kΩ (Table 1-2): measure with a high-impedance meter or by null. Adjustment A5 R59 (1V ADJ, ±5 µV, Table 2-1 item 2).

testpoints.condition: IN CAL lit; 10V output calibrated first; 23 ± 5 °C
testpoints.source: Table 4-3 front panel row, Internal voltage measurements step 9 (p42); tolerance from Table 1-2 transfer uncertainty, 1.018V, 1 year: 12.0 ppm (p10)
testpoints.note: Table 4-3 prints 1.018000V dc, corrective action Output Divider***. Footnote ***: calibration of the 10V output affects calibration of this output - check and set 10V first. ±12 ppm (±12.2 µV) is Table 1-2's one-year transfer uncertainty (30 days: 1.5 ppm); a drift specification, not a printed test limit. Source impedance ≈1 kΩ. Adjustment A5 R58 (1.018V ADJ, ±50 µV, Table 2-1 item 1).

Rear-panel black banana jack (A6 MP9), battery PCB terminal E2, reaching the - battery bus through CR1 in parallel with R1 51K. From Rev C a 3-pin connector J10 (pin 2 = -) replaces the jacks (Errata Change #5/#6).

testpoints.condition: Battery installed; no external source connected (reading the battery); high-impedance meter (Multimeter A)
testpoints.hazard: The battery assembly is capable of generating extremely high peak currents - avoid accidental shorting of battery terminals (§4-51)
testpoints.source: Table 4-3 rear panel row, Internal voltage measurements step 10 (p42); §2-21 (p17)
testpoints.note: Table 4-3: ≥24V dc, corrective action Battery. Rear-panel red banana jack (A6 MP8), battery PCB terminal E1, which reaches the battery + end (E3) through the ballast lamp DS1 - the BATTERY OPR switch is not in this path, so the battery reads here with the switch OFF. §2-21: the battery voltage may be measured at the POWER INPUT jacks with a high impedance multimeter such as Multimeter A. Related figures: 24 V nominal (four 6 V cells); permanent damage below 19 V (§2-22 CAUTION); charger ends constant-current charge at approximately 32V (§3-28; §4-44 step 21 and Errata §4-45d say above 31 V) and then holds approximately 27V at 23°C (§3-28); Errata #12 step 27: trickle-charge voltage 25.8-27 V at J10 with a known-good pack. External source limits: 24-40V dc or 24-30V ac 50-400 Hz (Table 1-2), floating source only, never tied to a front-panel terminal of the same unit (Figure 8-2 CAUTION). From Rev C the reading is taken at connector J10, pin 1 = +.
System copy of A3 TP4: the low lead for TP3 and TP6. On Figure 8-3 the return line joining C1 (-), C2, C3 (+) and the R3 / R4 left ends; on Figure 8-1 drawn on the -RAW line to P3-8.
System copy of A3 TP1: the -BATTERY bus (P3 pins 17/18, to A6 P4-2 and A4 P2-21/22). Low lead for TP2 and TP5, and for every §4-44 charger measurement.

testpoints.condition: Line power at the voltage marked on the rear panel
testpoints.hazard: MAINS - high voltage ac in the AC Module around the line connector, fuseholder and transformer (§4-51)
testpoints.note: Table 4-3: ≤60V dc; corrective action AC line voltage, Rectifier, Power Transformer. System copy of A3 TP3 (+ output of bridge CR1, top of C1, per Figure 8-3). Figure 8-1 mis-draws it: there TP3 hangs on the transformer secondary lead into the top (ac) vertex of the bridge, whose + output is the right vertex feeding R9 / CR19 - use Figure 8-3 (see caveat). A reading near zero with line applied points at the fuse, the line-voltage switches S1/S2, T1 or CR1; a reading above 60 V at the line-voltage setting.

testpoints.condition: Line power; battery charged or BATTERY OPR OFF
testpoints.note: Table 4-3: 32V dc, corrective action Pre-Regulator; no tolerance printed. ±1.6 V (5 %) is assumed - §3-11 says the emitter follower Q1 clamps the rectified power to approximately 32V dc. System copy of A3 TP6 (Q1 emitter after R1 0.5 Ω, the +RAW line to A4 P2-13/14 via A2 J3-2 / J2-13).

testpoints.condition: Battery installed, BATTERY OPR switch ON (Table 4-3 footnote **); line power
testpoints.source: Table 4-3, Internal voltage measurements step 3 (p42); §4-44 steps 16-21 (p38)
testpoints.note: Table 4-3: ≤31V dc, corrective action Battery Charger**. System copy of A3 TP2 (charger output between the W1 jumper and R11, feeding +BATTERY through CR13/CR16). §4-44 gives the behaviour behind the limit: BTRY CHG lights and constant-current charge starts at about 26 V (24.5-26.5 V), ends above 31 V, after which Q6 trickle-charges at about 27 V at 23 °C (§3-28). A reading over 31 V with BTRY CHG lit means the threshold set by R10 is off.

testpoints.condition: Battery installed, BATTERY OPR switch ON (Table 4-3 footnote **); line power at the marked voltage. §4-44 step 10 sets it under different conditions: W1 still installed (it is removed at step 12), BATTERY OPR OFF (step 2, ON again at step 15), a 50 kΩ rheostat at maximum between TP1 and TP2 (step 6), ac power through the Variac at the marked line voltage
testpoints.source: Table 4-3, Internal voltage measurements step 4 (p42); §4-44 step 10 (p38)
testpoints.note: Table 4-3: 33.0V dc, corrective action Battery Charger**; no tolerance printed. ±0.5 V is assumed, the same figure the A3 dataset uses for this point (the manual prints the value to a tenth of a volt but publishes no limit; §4-44 step 10: adjust R20 for a 33.0V dc reading). System copy of A3 TP5: the Q6 BASE node, where CR28 (current-regulator diode from the raw supply), R16 (from the Q6 emitter), R17 / RT1 (down through R18 and R20 to -BATTERY) and C6 meet - read off Figures 8-3 and 8-1, both of which draw TP5 on the lead perpendicular to Q6's base bar; the emitter (arrow) leaves through CR16 to +BATTERY and the collector is fed through R4 / CR20. Figure 8-1 letters the pot that sets it "R50": it is R20.
System copy of A4 TP3: the regulator's negative input rail (P2-23/24 -RAW, 21/22 -BATTERY), the Q4 series-pass side. Low lead for the 32 V check of TP1.

System copy of A4 TP2: the instrument COMMON (ground symbol), strapped to P2-2 -TEMP REG, P2-3 -BRIDGE, P2-4 -REF and P2-20 (IN CAL LED -), and so to A5 E1/E2/E3 and the front-panel LO. Low lead for the 18.5 V check of TP1.

System copy of A4 TP1, on the line Figure 8-1 letters 18.6V (P2 pins 12/13/14; P2-13/14 = +RAW from A3 P3-2). Table 4-3 reads it against two different low leads, so it carries two states: 32 V above TP3 (-RAW) proves the pre-regulator and the motherboard path; ≈18.5 V above TP2 (COMMON) proves the regulator, whose pass transistor Q4 sits between COMMON and -RAW (Figure 8-1: -RAW - Q4 - COMMON - P2-3). Figure 3-1 and §3-4 say 18.5V dc, §3-13 and the sheets 18.6V.

states.label: vs TP3 (-RAW): pre-regulator and motherboard
states.note: Table 4-3: 32V dc, corrective action Pre-Regulator, Motherboard; no tolerance printed, ±1.6 V (5 %) assumed as for A3 TP6. If A3 TP6 reads 32 V and this does not, the path A3 P3-2 - A2 J3-2 - J2-13/14 - A4 P2-13/14 (or the return P3-8 - J3-8 - J2-23/24) is open.

states.label: vs TP2 (COMMON): regulator output
states.note: Table 4-3: ≈18.5V dc, corrective action Regulator; printed with ≈ and no tolerance, ±0.5 V assumed - the same figure the A4 dataset uses, a band that contains the 18.6 V the sheets and §3-13 print. Below the critical value the voltage monitor Q8/Q5 shuts down the oven controller and latches IN CAL off (§3-15, 3-16).

testpoints.note: Motherboard test point on the heater terminal E1: the +HEATER / +TEMP REG line from A4 P2-10/11 (the 18.6 V supply) to the four heater wires. No table in the manual gives a value; the oven controller drives the heater return through A4 Q13/Q14, so the voltage across TP1-TP2 is whatever the loop demands (48 ± 2 °C oven, §3-23). From Rev C the thermal fuse F2 (58 °C) is in this lead (Errata Change #7).

Motherboard test point on the heater terminal E2: the return from HR1-HR4 to A4 P2-1 (HEATER), which on Figure 8-4 is the EMITTER of the PNP output transistor Q14 (its collector goes to COMMON; Q13 drives its base from HEAT DRIVE P2-26 through R26, with R24 / R25 as base-emitter resistors), through a dashed jumper symbol on Figure 8-2. No published value. Table 4-2 "Temperature sensitive - Oven - Check oven controller circuit": this pair is where the heater drive can be seen without opening the oven.

probePoints.label: OVEN TEMP THERMISTOR posts (A5 RT2)
probePoints.condition: Oven at operating temperature (48 ± 2 °C), IN CAL lit; ohmmeter (Multimeter A, 20 kΩ range) across the two white posts
probePoints.source: §2-35 (p18); §4-30 Acceptance Test item 3 (p32); Figure 8-1 "OVEN TEMP THMS" and Figure 8-5 "RT2 10K 25°C" (p85, p93)
probePoints.note: A resistance, not a voltage: the manual publishes no voltage at these posts. §2-35: the nominal value is between 3 kΩ and 4 kΩ at the normal oven operating temperature, temperature coefficient 3.8 %/°C, the actual operating value is shipped with the instrument. §4-30 item 3: within ±1 ohm of the value shipped with the instrument. RT2 is 10 kΩ at 25 °C (Figure 8-5). Errata #3: record the value to three significant digits whenever the 732A is used, daily otherwise; ±20 Ω day to day indicates probable oven problems, ±100 Ω short term affects the 1.0 and 1.018 V outputs appreciably. Both leads are isolated from all other circuitry; 60 V maximum to any other terminal (§2-34). Wired by W4 (GRA, GRA) from A5 E21/E22 to posts E8/E9.
